outcome: On 19-20 July 2026, Levent Alpöge (an Anthropic technical staff member) announced on X an explicit polynomial map F: C^3 -> C^3 with constant Jacobian determinant -2 (three degree-7 components) that sends three distinct points to the same image, disproving the Jacobian conjecture in dimension 3 and, by a standard stabilization argument (append the identity on extra coordinates), in every dimension n >= 3. The n=1 case was already trivially true and the planar (n=2) case remains open. Alpöge credited the construction to Anthropic's Claude Fable 5. The counterexample was independently checked by computer algebra within a day, digested mathematically by Terence Tao, and independently formalized in Lean 4 and in Isabelle (Archive of Formal Proofs), meeting the resolved bar via expert digestion plus independent machine-checked verification even though no journal has yet published it.

counterexample.object: Explicit polynomial map F=(P,Q,R): C^3 -> C^3 with P=(1+xy)^3 z + y^2(1+xy)(4+3xy), Q=y+3x(1+xy)^2 z+3xy^2(4+3xy), R=2x-3x^2y-x^3z, with det(J_F) identically -2, and with three distinct explicit rational points (e.g. (0,0,-1/4), (1,-3/2,13/2), (-1,3/2,13/2)) mapping to the same image (-1/4,0,0).
counterexample.verified_how: Independently checked by exact/symbolic computer algebra by multiple mathematicians within a day of announcement; independently formalized and machine-checked in Lean 4 (independent verification, and separately by Paul Lezeau, submitted to Google DeepMind's Formal Conjectures repository) and in Isabelle/HOL (Archive of Formal Proofs entry), plus a digestion/explanation by Terence Tao.

disputes.summary: Alexander Borisov, Ofer Gabber and Adrian Vasiu published a preprint ('On endomorphisms of affine spaces and the Jacobian problem', arXiv:2609.05746) with a 'Supplemental AI statement of the third author [Vasiu]' raising the concern that an earlier, unpublished version of their framework may have been included in the training data of frontier AI models and could have informed Fable's construction of the counterexample without proper credit. Commentary (e.g. Benjamin Collas and Gro-Tsen on X) framed this as part of a broader pattern of AI labs allegedly training on unpublished drafts/private communications across several 2026 conjecture resolutions (Jacobian, non-sofic groups, Navier-Stokes) without disclosing or crediting the source material. Alpöge subsequently stated on X that Borisov, Gabber and Vasiu 'deserve credit too.' I was not able to read the Vasiu PDF's exact statement directly (fetch failed to extract readable text and Bash access to convert it was not authorized), so this is based on secondary reporting (DataCamp; Fortune) and X posts describing the preprint's content, not a direct reading of page 160 of that preprint.

summary: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician on Anthropic's technical staff, announced on X on 19 July 2026 (a 'very casual' post reading 'hello there the jacobian conjecture is false thanx to my close friend akhil for asking about it and my other close friend fable for working during the world cup final') an explicit degree-7 polynomial counterexample in C^3 to the Jacobian conjecture, disproving it for n=3 and, by trivial extension (identity on extra coordinates), for all n>=3; the n=1 case was already known true and n=2 (the planar Jacobian conjecture) remains open. He credited the construction itself to Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic). Multiple independent sources (John D. Cook, Terence Tao, Fortune, DataCamp, The Conversation, Kevin Buzzard's Xena blog) corroborate that the AI produced the actual construction/search result while Alpöge posed the question and announced/verified it -- DataCamp's framing 'a human posed the question, an AI did the work, a human announced the result' matches Alpöge's own phrasing crediting Fable with 'working' on it. No source I found discloses the actual prompts or the human-AI interaction log, so the fine-grained division of labor within that process is not publicly documented, but the authors' own account (Alpöge's post) squarely credits the AI system with producing the mathematical construction, supporting ai_role=generated rather than assisted. The result was verified extremely quickly: computer-algebra checks within hours/a day, a mathematical digestion by Terence Tao explaining why the construction works, and at least two independent formal verifications (a Lean 4 formalization, and a separate Isabelle/HOL Archive-of-Formal-Proofs entry proving the Jacobian is identically -2 and that three named points share an image), plus a Lean formalization submitted to DeepMind's Formal Conjectures repository. This combination of expert digestion (Tao) and independent machine-checkable verification meets the bar for status=resolved under Sec 6.1 even though, as of the sources found (through mid-September 2026), no traditional journal has yet published a refereed version -- it remains, in one source's words, 'a verified calculation and a preprint, not a refereed paper.' Multiple follow-up arXiv papers (Shuhong Gao, arXiv:2608.00222; T. Shaska, arXiv:2607.20210, 'Graded Keller maps and the Jacobian Conjecture'; Arno van den Essen, arXiv:2609.17795, showing an 'elementary' route to essentially the same example) generalize or re-derive the construction, and a Zenodo preprint traces downstream consequences for several related conjectures (Mathieu, Dixmier, Poisson, Gaussian moments). A priority dispute emerged: Borisov, Gabber and Vasiu's preprint (arXiv:2609.05746) includes a 'supplemental AI statement' suggesting their earlier unpublished framework may have been absorbed into AI training data and used without credit in reaching the counterexample; Alpöge reportedly acknowledged on X that they 'deserve credit too.' I could not directly read that supplemental statement (PDF text extraction failed via WebFetch, and Bash commands to download/convert it were not authorized in this session), so the dispute is recorded from secondary reporting and social-media commentary rather than the primary document -- flagged in confidence and in the dispute entry. The n=2 case is untouched by any of this and remains open with no result found addressing it in the window.
competing_reading: One could argue ai_role should be 'assisted' rather than 'generated', since no source discloses the actual prompt/interaction transcript, and it is conceivable Alpöge did substantial guiding work (choice of ansatz, search space design) that is simply not reported. The Conversation explicitly notes 'details have not been made public regarding exactly how Alpöge prompted the AI model.' However, the balance of direct evidence -- Alpöge's own words crediting Fable with 'working' on it, and multiple secondary sources' explicit framing that the AI produced the construction while Alpöge only posed the question and announced the result -- favors 'generated.' If a more detailed account later emerges showing Alpöge did the core mathematical construction and merely used the AI to check steps, this should be revised to 'assisted' or 'none'.
what_would_settle_it: Publication of Alpöge's own detailed writeup or interaction transcript describing exactly what he prompted and what Fable returned; alternatively, a technical report from Anthropic describing the episode (as has happened for other AI-math results) would settle both the ai_role classification and the priority dispute with Borisov-Gabber-Vasiu regarding training-data provenance. A referee report or journal acceptance would also move status language from 'resolved-by-community-verification' to an unambiguous formal resolution, though this does not change the classification here.
